label: Home
heading: Home
lede: Welcome back, admin@example.com.

label: Payouts
heading: Orders
lede: What each payment method charged over the window, what went back out through it, and what it is still owed. A sale here means the same as on Reports: an order whose stock has left the shelf.

label: Inventory
heading: Inventory
lede: Available is on hand minus what is reserved for orders in flight. Stock moves as a delta or an absolute count, never as a blind overwrite — so a sale that lands mid-edit cannot be lost. Without a location chosen, the thr

label: Customers
heading: Customers
lede: A cancelled order is still an order but not a sale, and money only counts once it has arrived — so the two figures rarely match.

label: Groups
heading: Customers
lede: A shopper joins a group on their customer record; the price lists that aim at it are under Products.

label: Setup Email
heading: Notifications
lede: Who carries the store's emails. Activate a provider and type its key; until one is active every message is written to the log and nobody receives it.

label: Setup SMS
heading: Notifications
lede: Who carries the store's texts. Activate a provider and type its key; until one is active every message is written to the log and nobody receives it.

label: Files
heading: Media
lede: Drag and drop images, videos, 3D models, and files

label: Menus
heading: Menus
lede: Pick a menu on the left, or create one. A storefront reads a menu from /x/navigation/menus/<handle>.

label: Product feeds
heading: Content
lede: Both files are generated when they are fetched, from the catalogue as it stands at that moment. There is no build to schedule and nothing to regenerate.

label: Sitemap
heading: Content
lede: Read by fetching the files themselves, the way a crawler would. Each is generated at the moment it is asked for, so what is counted here is exactly what a crawler would have got a second ago.

label: FAQ
heading: Content
lede: The questions this shop is asked often, grouped into the sections you name and in the order you put them. A draft is invisible to shoppers. The storefront reads the published ones from /x/faq.

label: Reports
heading: Reports
lede: Sales — what the store sold, by period, with its best sellers — is on the dashboard. This is for the questions only this shop has, written as SQL once and run by whoever needs the answer.

label: Jobs
heading: Jobs
lede: The full outbox, with every event's history, is under Settings › Event log.

label: Plugins
heading: Plugins
lede: A line across the top of every storefront page — a promotion, a notice, a shipping threshold.

label: Payment methods
heading: Settings
lede: How shoppers pay. A gateway that is active and set up is offered at checkout; an idle one is listed here and nowhere else. Cash on delivery is built in.

label: Shipping and delivery
heading: Settings
lede: The most specific zone wins: a zone naming a state beats one naming only its country, which beats the zone that names nowhere in particular.

label: Shipping providers
heading: Shipping
lede: Who carries the parcels. An aggregator that is active and set up is offered on the ship dialog; an idle one is listed here and nowhere else. Manual fulfilment is built in.

label: Diagnostics
heading: Settings
lede: Nothing has failed, but 3 checks of 15 are worth a look.

label: API keys
heading: Settings
lede: A key is held to its role exactly as a person is, so give it the smallest one that does the job. Owner includes making more keys.

label: Webhooks
heading: Settings
lede: Where this store POSTs the events an endpoint names. Each delivery is signed, and a failed one is retried on a backoff until it is delivered or given up on.

label: Import
heading: Settings
lede: A dry run validates the whole file and rolls back, reporting what it would have done. Worth doing first, always.
